Agreement No. CA-2025-03. This Consignment Agreement is made between Juniper Lane Mercantile (the Shop) and Caleb
Acosta, doing business as Hollow Oak Pottery (the Consignor). The Consignor wishes the Shop to display and sell the
handmade goods listed on the Schedule of Consigned Items.

1. Term
This Agreement begins 05/17/2025 and ends 11/16/2025. It renews for successive three-month periods unless either party
gives written notice at least thirty days before the end of the then-current period. Either party may end this Agreement earlier
on thirty days written notice.

2. Title and Risk of Loss
The consigned goods remain the property of the Consignor until sold. The Shop will display them with reasonable care in the
main sales area. The Shop is not responsible for loss caused by fire, theft or damage; however, if goods are lost or damaged
by an employee while in the Shop's custody, the Shop will pay the Consignor 50% of the retail price. The Consignor should
insure the goods at the Consignor's own expense.

3. Pricing and Display
The Consignor sets the retail price of each item, shown on the Schedule. Price changes must be requested in writing. The
Shop may mark items down by up to twenty percent during store-wide promotions, and the Consignor's share is then
calculated on the actual selling price. The Shop decides placement and may rotate items.

4. Commission and Payment
When an item sells, the Consignor receives 60% of the selling price before sales tax and the Shop keeps 40%. The Shop will
send a written statement of sales and pay the amount due by the 15th of each month for sales in the prior month, by check. If
the amount due is less than $25, the Shop may carry it forward to the next month.

5. Delivery, Inventory and Unsold Goods
The Consignor will deliver items clean, finished, labeled and ready to display. The Shop will keep a record of every item
received and will give the Consignor a signed copy. Items unsold at the end of the Agreement must be picked up within 45
days after the end date; after that the Shop may donate them to charity or dispose of them.

6. Quality, Taxes and Legal Compliance
The Consignor represents that the goods are the Consignor's own original work, do not infringe anyone's rights, and meet all
safety and labeling laws, including labeling for soaps and food-contact goods. The Shop collects and remits sales tax on retail
sales. The Consignor is an independent business and is responsible for its own income taxes.

7. General
This is the entire agreement about the consigned goods and may be changed only in writing signed by both parties. It is
governed by the laws of Tennessee.

1. The Contract Documents
The Contract Documents consist of this Contract, the Schedule of Values attached as Exhibit A, the plans and specifications identified in the bid proposal, addenda, and any written change orders signed by both parties. In the event of a conflict, the signed change order controls, followed by this Contract, then the plans, then the specifications.
2. Scope of Work
Contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, supervision and permits necessary to complete the work for Summit - Office Remodel at the Project Site shown above, as described in the Contract Documents. Work not described in the Contract Documents is excluded unless added by change order.
3. Contract Sum
Owner shall pay Contractor the stipulated sum of $782,000.00, subject to additions and deductions made by written change order. The Contract Sum includes all taxes applicable to the work as of the Contract Date.
4. Progress Payments
Contractor shall submit a monthly Application for Payment based on the Schedule of Values for work completed through the last day of each month. Owner shall pay each approved application within 20 days of receipt. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at 1.5% per month until paid. Contractor shall furnish a lien waiver for each progress payment received.
5. Retainage
Owner may withhold 10% of each progress payment as retainage. Retainage shall be released within 10 days after Substantial Completion, receipt of final lien waivers from Contractor and each subcontractor, and completion of the punch list.
6. Time of Performance
Contractor shall commence the work on 3/31/25 and achieve Substantial Completion by 9/30/25, subject to extension for change orders, weather, delays by Owner or the Architect, material shortages and other causes beyond Contractor's control. If Contractor fails to achieve Substantial Completion by the date stated, as extended, Owner may assess liquidated damages of $500.00 per calendar day as Owner's sole remedy for delay.
7. Changes in the Work
Owner may order changes in the work. No change is valid unless in writing and signed by Owner and Contractor, stating the adjustment to the Contract Sum and Contract Time. Changes will be priced at Contractor's actual cost plus 10% for overhead and profit unless a lump sum is agreed. Contractor is not required to proceed with extra work until a change order is signed.
8. Permits, Inspections and Code Compliance

Part 2 of 3
Contractor shall obtain the building permit and arrange inspections required by the jurisdiction. Fees for the building permit are included in the Contract Sum. Owner is responsible for utility connection charges, impact fees and special inspection fees not included in the Schedule of Values.
9. Insurance
Contractor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with limits of at least $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, automobile liability insurance, and workers compensation insurance as required by law, and shall furnish certificates of insurance upon request. Owner shall maintain property insurance on the structure during construction.
10. Subcontractors
Contractor may perform the work with its own forces or through licensed subcontractors of its choosing. Contractor remains responsible for the work of its subcontractors and shall require each to furnish lien waivers and certificates of insurance.
11. Warranty
Contractor warrants that the work will be free from defects in workmanship for a period of one year from Substantial Completion. Manufacturer warranties on equipment and materials are assigned to Owner. This warranty does not cover damage from misuse, lack of maintenance, ordinary wear, or acts of nature.
12. Owner's Responsibilities
Owner shall furnish timely access to the site, make timely decisions on selections and allowances, and pay the Contract Sum as provided herein. Delays caused by late selections or access will extend the Contract Time.
13. Hidden or Unforeseen Conditions
If concealed or unknown conditions are encountered that differ materially from those indicated in the Contract Documents, including soil conditions, hazardous materials or deteriorated structure, Contractor shall notify Owner promptly and the Contract Sum and Contract Time shall be adjusted by change order.
14. Termination
Either party may terminate this Contract for the other's material breach if the breach is not cured within seven days after written notice. If Owner terminates for convenience, Owner shall pay Contractor for work completed, materials ordered, and reasonable overhead and profit on the work not performed. Contractor may suspend work if payment is not made when due.
15. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
The parties shall first attempt to resolve disputes by good-faith negotiation and then by non-binding mediation before commencing legal proceedings. This Contract is governed by the laws of the State of Arizona. The prevailing party in any action to enforce this Contract may recover reasonable attorney fees and costs.
16. Entire Agreement
This Contract is the entire agreement between the parties and may be modified only by a writing signed by both. Notices must be in writing and delivered to the addresses shown above.

This Grant Agreement is made on 2025-03-12 between Westfield Health Foundation (the Funder) and Harborlight Neighbors Alliance (the
Grantee) with respect to Grant No. AW-25-1471.

1. Purpose of the Grant
The Funder awards the Grantee a grant of 120,000.00 to be used exclusively for the Senior Lunch Program (the Project), as described in the
Grantee's proposal dated before the award letter. The grant may not be used for any other purpose, for lobbying, for political campaign activity, or
for religious instruction, and no part of the grant may be re-granted without the Funder's written consent.

2. Grant Period
The grant period begins 2025-03-22 and ends 2027-03-21. Funds not spent by the end of the grant period must be returned to the Funder within 30
days unless the Funder has approved an extension in writing before that date.

3. Payment Schedule
The Funder will pay the grant in the installments shown below. Each installment after the first is conditioned on the Funder's written acceptance of
the report named in the table and on the Grantee remaining in compliance with this Agreement.

Installment   Condition   Scheduled Payment Date   Amount
Initial payment   Upon signed agreement   2025-03-26   60,000.00
Final payment   Upon acceptance of interim report   2026-01-21   60,000.00

4. Reporting Requirements
The Grantee will submit an interim program and financial report on or before 2025-12-22, and a final program and financial report on or before
2027-04-20. Each report must describe progress against the goals and outcome measures in the proposal, report the number of people served, and
compare actual spending with the approved Project budget. The Funder may withhold any payment while a report is overdue.

5. Budget and Allowable Costs
Grant funds must be spent in substantial accordance with the approved Project budget. The Grantee may move up to ten percent of any budget line

This Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) sets out how Beacon Community Church and the Alliance will work
together on the Senior Lunch Program from 2025-04-21 through 2026-04-20. It is a statement of cooperation and does
not create a binding obligation to pay money.
1. Responsibilities of the Partner
The Partner will make its space available for the program for 4 hours per week, will designate one staff or volunteer
liaison, will help publicize the program to the families and residents it serves, and will keep the space clean and safe.

The Alliance will provide program staff and trained volunteers, food and supplies, and liability insurance for the
program, will keep attendance records, and will share summary results with the Partner at the review meeting on
2025-10-21.
3. Privacy
Each party will keep personal information about participants confidential and will share it only as needed to run the
program. Neither party will use participant information for fundraising without written permission.
4. Term and Ending This MOU
This MOU begins 2025-04-21 and ends 2026-04-20 unless extended in writing. Either party may end it on 60 days
written notice.
5. Independent Parties
The parties are independent organizations. Neither is the agent or employee of the other, and each is responsible for
its own staff, volunteers and insurance. No money passes between the parties under this MOU; any in-kind support will
be recorded separately.

This Lease is made between Granite Commercial Properties Inc. (Landlord) and Juniper Lane Mercantile (Tenant) for retail space in
the shopping center identified above.

1. Premises and Term
Landlord leases to Tenant Unit 6, containing approximately 1,443 square feet (the Premises), for a term of 60 months beginning
12/31/2023 and ending 12/30/2028. Tenant may use the common parking areas on a non-exclusive basis with other tenants and their
customers.

2. Base Rent
Tenant shall pay monthly base rent of $4,100.00, due in advance on the first day of each month without demand. Base rent increases
3% on each anniversary of the start date. A late charge of $100.00 applies to any payment received more than five days after its due
date, and returned payments carry an additional handling fee.

3. Percentage Rent
If Tenant's annual gross sales from the Premises exceed $600,000.00, Tenant shall pay additional rent equal to 6% of the excess.
Tenant shall deliver a statement of gross sales within sixty days after the end of each lease year, and Landlord may inspect Tenant's
sales tax returns to verify it.

4. Common Area and Other Charges
Tenant pays its proportionate share of common area maintenance, property taxes, and landlord's insurance, currently estimated at
$202.02 per month, reconciled annually. Tenant pays for its own utilities, telephone and internet, and for waste removal.

5. Security Deposit
Tenant has deposited $4,100.00 as a security deposit, to be held by Landlord without interest and returned within thirty days after the
end of the term, less lawful deductions for unpaid rent and damage beyond normal wear.

6. Use; Hours of Operation
Tenant shall use the Premises as a retail shop selling gifts, home goods, stationery, foods and locally made products, and for no
other purpose without Landlord's consent. Tenant shall be open for business at least five days a week and shall keep its display
windows lighted until 9:00 PM. Tenant shall not conduct going-out-of-business sales.

7. Signs
Tenant may install one storefront sign and one pylon panel conforming to the center's sign criteria, at Tenant's cost, with Landlord's
prior written approval. Tenant shall remove its signs at the end of the term and repair any damage.

8. Maintenance and Repairs
Tenant shall keep the interior of the Premises, including the storefront glass, doors, floor coverings, lighting and Tenant's fixtures, in
good condition. Landlord shall maintain the roof, structure, exterior walls, parking areas and common utility lines. Tenant is
responsible for servicing the rooftop heating and cooling unit serving the Premises.

9. Alterations
Tenant shall make no alteration other than the installation of trade fixtures and shelving without Landlord's written consent.
Alterations become Landlord's property unless Landlord requires removal at the end of the term.

10. Insurance and Indemnity
Tenant shall carry commercial general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence naming Landlord as additional
insured, and property insurance on its inventory, fixtures and improvements. Tenant shall indemnify Landlord against claims arising
from Tenant's use of the Premises except those caused by Landlord's negligence.

Tenant may not assign this Lease or sublet the Premises without Landlord's written consent, which Landlord shall not unreasonably

SUBCONTRACT AGREEMENT
SC-130 - Solar Racking
Subcontract # | SC-130 | Agreement Date | 5/31/25
WO # | 25104 | Subcontract Price | 50,000.00
Completion Date | 7/6/25 | Retainage | 10%
CONTRACTOR / Summit Line Electric / 8916 Redwood Rd / Lakewood, CO 80204 | SUBCONTRACTOR / Ridgeline Solar Racking Company / Attn: Teresa Mata / 515 N Willow Way / Denver, CO 80283
1. Scope of Work
Subcontractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment and supervision required to perform the Solar Racking work for the project known as Site lighting and power, located at 9776 Heritage Rd, Bldg 163, Denver, CO 80263, in accordance with the plans, specifications and addenda in the Contractor's contract with the Owner, which are incorporated by reference. Work outside the written scope requires a signed change order before it is performed.
2. Subcontract Price and Payment
Contractor shall pay Subcontractor the Subcontract Price of 50,000.00, subject to additions and deductions by change order. Subcontractor shall submit monthly applications for payment with a schedule of values. Contractor shall pay the approved amount within 14 days after Contractor receives payment from the Owner for that work, less retainage at the rate shown above. Payment to Subcontractor is conditioned on receipt of a conditional lien waiver with each application and an unconditional waiver for the prior payment.
3. Retainage
Retainage withheld from each payment is released within thirty days after final completion of the Subcontractor's work, final inspection approval, delivery of record drawings and warranties, and a final unconditional lien waiver, whichever is last.
4. Schedule and Delays
Time is of the essence. Subcontractor shall achieve completion by the date shown above and shall coordinate its work with other trades through the Contractor's superintendent. If completion is delayed for reasons within Subcontractor's control, Contractor may deduct liquidated damages of 500.00 per calendar day, which the parties agree is a reasonable estimate of Contractor's losses.
5. Insurance
Subcontractor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with limits of at least 1,000,000.00 per occurrence, automobile liability, workers compensation as required by law, and umbrella coverage, and shall deliver certificates naming Contractor and Owner as additional insureds before starting work. Subcontractor shall give Contractor written notice before any coverage is cancelled or reduced.
6. Indemnity
To the fullest extent permitted by law, Subcontractor shall indemnify and hold harmless Contractor and Owner from claims, damages, losses and expenses, including reasonable attorney fees, arising out of Subcontractor's work to the extent caused by its negligence or that of anyone for whom it is responsible.
7. Safety

Part 2 of 2
Subcontractor shall comply with all applicable safety laws and with Contractor's site safety program, shall hold a pre-task safety meeting for its crew each day, and shall ensure that its employees hold current training records. Contractor may remove any worker who violates safety rules from the site.
8. Changes and Back-charges
Contractor may order changes in the work. Subcontractor shall submit its price for any change within five working days. Contractor may back-charge Subcontractor for cleanup, repairs to damage caused by Subcontractor, or work Subcontractor fails to perform, after 3 days written notice to cure.
9. Warranty
Subcontractor warrants its work against defects in materials and workmanship for one year from final acceptance, and shall promptly correct defective work at its own cost. Manufacturer warranties on equipment shall be assigned to the Owner.
10. Termination
Contractor may terminate this Subcontract for default if Subcontractor fails to cure a material breach within 7 days after written notice, and may complete the work with its own forces or others and charge the excess cost to Subcontractor. Contractor may also terminate for convenience on written notice, paying for work performed and reasonable demobilization.
11. Disputes and General
Disputes shall be resolved first by negotiation between principals, then by mediation, before suit is filed in the county where the project is located. This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of Colorado and is the entire agreement between the parties; it may be modified only in writing signed by both parties, and neither party may assign it without written consent.
